recipes.name: Grandma Jensen’s Nuts and Bolts
ingredients_raw: 2 cups bite-size wheat square cereal (such as Wheat Chex®)
2 cups bite-size corn square cereal (such as Corn Chex®)
2 cups bite-size rice square cereal (such as Rice Chex®)
2 cups toasted oat cereal rings (such as Cheerios®)

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 225 degrees F (110 degrees C). Combine the wheat cereal, corn cereal, rice cereal, oat cereal, cheese-flavored crackers, pretzels, and mixed nuts in a large bowl; set aside.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the garlic powder and Worcestershire sauce until evenly blended.
Pour over the cereal mixture, and gently stir until the cereal is evenly coated with the seasoned butter.
Spread the cereal mixture onto baking sheets, and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes. Allow to cool to room temperature before storing in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma Jensen’s Nuts and Bolts
raw_recipe.description: Garlic powder and Worcestershire sauce flavor this common holiday snack mix.

review.reviewBody: Can't go wrong w/ a classic, crunchy snack mix! I used what I had on hand (baby Goldfish, corn Chex, pretzel Goldfish, peanuts) - I scrapped the Cheerios b/c last time I baked those in a snack mix, they shriveled up to teeny, tiny little "O"s. I went a bit lighter on the butter, and for personal preference, added a shake of ground coriander and onion powder. Baking time is dead-on (don't forget to stir!), and upon cooling, I scooped in some golden raisins and mini M&Ms'. I am tossing handfuls of "Nuts & Bolts" in my mouth as I type this. /crunch. Thanks for an alternative to store-bought bags of Chex Mix!

I am rating this on the proportion of snack mix to garlic butter mixture, as it is spot on. everything was evenly coated before going into the oven, and therefore each piece was seasoned well. I changed up the mix but kept the snack mix portion to 16 cups total. rice, corn chex, crunchy cheezits, butter pretzels, bugles, peanuts, walnuts, snyder pretzel pieces in buffalo wing, and honey mustard onion. I did add 2 tsp onion powder, and some soul food seasoning to the butter as well as the garlic powder. this combination got rave reviews and everyone asked me for the recipe because it was so different than the usual. All I did was go up and down the snack/chip aisle of the grocery and perused through what I thought seemed like it could be put into this. I had a lot of fun making this due to the variations. thanks so much. such a nice anytime mix, party mix, holiday treat.
Have made this several times, using 2/3 cup butter and vary the seasonings to taste. My family likes some smoky flavour.

My family has made a similiar mix for years but we add a package of onion soup mix (or for garlic lovers - onion and roasted garlic soup mix) to melting butter. I also toast everything except the cheese crackers, and add them when the mix is cooled. Try some hickory potato sticks too.

Simple to make and great taste! I substituted 2 cups of cereal for Grissol Baguette pieces and used 1 1/2 tsp of garlic salt, 1/2 tsp onion salt, and 1/2 tsp celery salt. I also used a disposable roasting pan which was the perfect size! Will definitely make again.

I omitted nuts, because expensive. I used Crispix, instead of rice and corn chex, and non one likes wheat chex, so I left that out too. I added more crispix, cheerios, and pretzels to make up the difference. I exchanged one tablespoon Worcestershire sauce for one of balsamic vinegar. Very yummy, and much more inexpensive. Less variety, but I'm still looking for more things we like better to add in.

Very good recipe. I added some chili powder and onion powder for a little extra flavour. Big hit. Also for a nice twist, omit the cheese crackers and use Asiago crackers available at Costco. Those are far more flavourful than Goldfish

Tasty recipe. I also used cheerios, wasabi pea's and celery salt.
As per one reviewer I will try it with a packet of onion soup mix next time.

This is the recipe I have used since the 60's. I double the recipe and make it in an aluminum roasting pan for the holidays. The only thing I do different is use equal amounts of garlic powder, onion powder and celery salt. Be careful not to use too much salt! Thank you for sharing this. I had lost my original recipe.
I have to agree. This is a ripoff recipe and not even the best version. Try one with some bacon grease if you are on the naughty list.
This is our any time of the year family favorite! instead of Chex I prefer Chrispix :) and end up nearly doubling the butter, W-sauce and garlic powder. So good!!

This is like my mom used to make! We use Cracklin Oat Bran instead of Cheerios and Chexmix instead of the corn and rice chex. The sweetness of the oat bran adds a great mix to the salt. That is my family's favorite part. I don't use any crackers or cheesy anything. I also soak my nuts in the butter mixture before tossing them into the cereal mixture. They absorb the seasoning better that way. I bake at 325 for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes as it browns it a little more. You want the cereal crispy. I add about 1-2 teaspoons of Cayenne pepper according to how spicy you like it and more worcestershire. I also double this if you want to have a lot around to snack on. Definitely a crowd pleaser. I have friends ask me every year if I am making my Texas Trash! Great snack!
Love that you call it Nuts and Bolts. That's what my mother called it, too. Nice twist with using Cheez It's.

This is the same recipe handed down to me from my grandmother. Thanks for sharing. The name comes from Cheerios (being the nuts) and pretzel sticks (being the bolts). No clue on its origin. I've made changes every year based upon feedback from the prior year. Adding much more Worcestershire and garlic is always a plus. Zero Cheez-Its. I was taught to bake it in the oven at 200 degrees for 20 minutes at a time. Take out of the oven and using a ladel, lift the mix from the bottom up. The butter goodness always drains down, and this insures everything gets covered evenly in that lovely (butter mixture). Do this 4 times. Then let it sit stove top and cool. Salt is key in this recipe (to me). Garlic salt makes a huge difference in taste. Lastly, use the leftover crumbs on a salad in place of croutons, in Mac and cheese or in vanilla ice cream. Yum! Try this original recipe, then consider making it your own. Either way, it will quickly become your families favorite snack (make tons as your friends and family will want some to take home). Enjoy, Mark
An Uprgrated Chex Mix Treat That Sounds Scrumdillicious!

Excellent basic recipe. I do tweak it a little with fresh minced garlic in the butter mixture instead of powdered and a healthy dash of Tabasco because I like the heat and flavor but this recipe can be tweaked a bit in this way to suit individual tastes without departing from the recipe entirely.
